content.text: Chorizo is a Uruguayan variant of the Spanish card game Escoba, featuring additional ways to capture cards and bonus scores for declaring combinations of cards in hand. The game is known for its lively, unpredictable nature with sudden changes of fortune. Some variants replace certain combinations with BÃ¡ciga rules.

Country/Region of Origin: Uruguay
Time Period: 20th century
Historical Development: Evolved from the Spanish game Escoba, brought to Uruguay by European immigrants. The game developed unique local characteristics, particularly the declaration bonuses and wild card mechanics.
Cultural Significance: Popular in Uruguay, especially in Montevideo and Flores. Some players simply call it Escoba.

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 4
Optimal Players: 2 or 4 (partnerships)
Partnerships: Yes for 4 players (partners opposite)

Type: Spanish 40-card deck
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included
Card Values: Ace=1, 2-7=face value, Sota (Jack)=8, Caballo (Horse)=9, Rey (King)=10

Spanish 40-card deck
Score sheet
Table space

Initial Deal: 3 cards to each player, 4 cards face-up to table
Subsequent Deals: 3 cards each when hands are empty (no more table cards)
Dealing Pattern: Counterclockwise
Direction: Counterclockwise play
